notes: 2026-09-10: Single run, slot 2 (product infrastructure, APIs, backend components) per deterministic date formula (day_of_year 253 % 7 + 1 = 2). Catalogued 5 new, all in-slot: Posthorn (craigmccaskill/posthorn, Apache-2.0, single-binary unified outbound-mail gateway for self-hosted apps — three ingress shapes into five provider transports, PROTOTYPE, 8.2 — the strongest find this run: narrow scope, unusually disciplined docs including an explicit 'what it is not' section), RustFS (rustfs/rustfs, Apache-2.0, S3-compatible distributed object storage explicitly positioned as the permissively-licensed MinIO alternative, PROTOTYPE, 7.9 — 31,915 stars but still pre-1.0, release-candidate tags only, tag history lags active development), Openpanel (Openpanel-dev/openpanel, AGPL-3.0 flagged loudly, mature self-hosted Mixpanel alternative, PROTOTYPE, 7.6), Convoy (frain-dev/convoy, Elastic License 2.0 flagged loudly — confirmed via raw LICENSE file after the GitHub API license field returned NOASSERTION, mature webhooks-delivery gateway est. 2021, PROTOTYPE, 7.4), and SQLite Sync (sqliteai/sqlite-sync, Elastic License 2.0 modified flagged loudly, CRDT-based offline-first SQLite sync extension with a Block-Level LWW mode aimed at multi-agent markdown editing, STUDY, 7.1 — genuinely usable against self-hosted Postgres/Supabase without the maker's paid cloud product, but is an explicit open-core funnel toward it). Notable pattern this run: three of five deep-reviewed candidates (Convoy, SQLite Sync, and rejected Notifuse) turned out to carry non-OSI source-available licenses (Elastic License 2.0 x2, BSL 1.1) that the GitHub API's license field either mis-reported as NOASSERTION or omitted — raw LICENSE-file verification via raw.githubusercontent.com caught all three; continue treating the API license field as a starting point, not a final answer, especially for gateway/infrastructure repos. Rejected Notifuse (BSL 1.1, same issue class as billabear 2026-08-29) and tigrisdata/storage (client SDKs only, not self-hostable — Tigris itself is a proprietary hosted service). Identified and skipped three same-day duplicate waves without itemizing every repo: a 'self-hosted email sending via AWS SES' wave (opensend, reloop, larasend — posthorn's provider-agnostic design was clearly the strongest of the group), an 'AI/LLM multi-provider gateway' wave (gpt-load, control-layer, modelship, voidllm, qwengate, Gozar, aurora — niche already saturated in this catalog via anythingmcp/mcp-compressor/Preloop), and a 'webhook capture/debug/replay' wave (webhook-tester, webhook-debugger-logger, inhook, webhook-debugger x2, stripeek, request-catcher — all sub-150-star, no standout maturity, and this niche already has a cautionary precedent with the archived viewhook from 2026-08-29). webhookx-io/webhookx (Apache-2.0 webhook gateway, cleaner license than Convoy but far less mature) and Kodiqa-Solutions/VaultS3 (AGPL-3.0 lightweight S3-alt, 1,598 stars) filed as Worth Watching.
